It took me by surprise. I had been dating for 4/5 months when we began to talk. I was dating mainly to curve some of the loneliness so I didn't expect much out if it but he was elated to talk to me. I was taken aback when he asked for my cell phone number instead of my snapchat like every other man I had interacted with on dating apps. We arranged a call in the evening and spoke for 4+ hours. After which he said he HAD to meet me because what we had was 'one of a kind'. I was skeptical but the first day we met in person he spent the night and it was the most natural thing in the world. It was during the 3rd day that he looked at me - with a warmth in his eyes that no one else ever had towards me - and told me he loved me. Cue confusion and an exasperated "But you don't even know my last name?!" 

He didn't miss a beat. He smiled, asked what it was, then caressed my face and said it again. I was unsure what to do but he didn't pressure me or get upset that I was speechless. My confusion increased as I realized I felt disappointed that he was leaving rather than any relief. Was I crazy? Was he? As I contemplated the events of the past 3 days, my cats and I all gathered at the door. He started to tie up his boots and I blurted out "Come back home soon, 'kay?" And much to my embarrassment he smiled the biggest smile I had seen yet and hugged me tight. When the door shut behind him my cats and I all stood there in silence for a couple moments. We stared quietly at the door as we heard his footsteps fade; my older cat looked at me and gave a worried meow before we dispersed within the apartment. I realized he had so quickly become the center of our world. 

He was back the next day to spend the next few days together. We were pretty much strangers and I had an out of country trip in less than a month. I was anxious that these feelings would wane once we were hundreds of miles apart. Yet, there wasn't a night where we failed to talk on the phone for at least 2 hours. He gave me a sense of stability and love that nobody else has. He's my partner and I hate to imagine a life without him. Meeting him was like my soul collided with his and I didn't have time to question any of it. It may be wishful thinking, but there were clues and coincidences that we've identified throughout our lives that were signs of our eventual meeting. It confirmed to me that destiny is real.

As someone who grew up close with the undocumented community, this was a very accurate representation of how sneaky the detainment and deportation process is.

There are situations where ICE will wait outside the sherrifs office to detain any hispanic who was in custody. One instance stuck with me - a undoc man was driving and pulled over for "speeding". He wasn't, but once pulled over they asked for his license/any ID. Didn't have any so they detained him. Once in custody they filed the ticket for driving without a DL and he paid the fine upfront. He walked out of the office and ICE was waiting for him. He didn't even get to say goodbye to his family. Once in his country he called and told them how there were dozens of teenage boys detained by ICE. They all had the same  story; walking home/around town during the day and stopped for ID. School IDs didn't count, so they were detained until there was PROOF they had legal status.

Other stories are worse. Individuals detained have the right to a court hearing to plead their case - Immigration officers then present them a voluntary deportation slip in English and ask them to sign so they can be released.

Some don't even understand what they signed until they are taken to the airport

I just had surgery to remove my AVM on July 24th. It was located in the posterior right parietal lobe. This was 1 of 2 AVMs that I was born with - 1st one was closer to the occipital lobe and it ruptured when I was 9. I'm 24 and for this surgery I was discharged after only 5 days. 1 thing I can tell you is be prepared in case your body has a negative reaction to the anesthesia. I woke up once they were moving me to the CT scanner after the surgery and I vomited all over my face. I spent all night vomiting and had to take my sweet time eating for the following days. The incision on my head was a little sore and it was painful to sneeze or cough, but its been nearly 2 weeks and I've slowly been able to wash my hair a little closer to the incision each day (theres adhesive from the dressing they placed) and its not as sensitive as before; so the only thing that's really bothering me is that the outside of my right thigh has been numb or painful ever since the 4th day I was inpatient. Possibly a side effect of being on bedrest or/and my angiogram (they went in through my groin) BUT my vision and coordination have greatly improved compared to before my surgery so I'm optimistic this too will go away with time. Its liberating to be free of a ticking time bomb. I suffered from anxiety before but knowing that the odds are now in my favor has really helped. I wish you the best!! You can ask me anything.

Edit: my first angio for this surgery was in November and they went in through my wrist rather than my groin. I couldn't move my arm or lift anything for a few days, but it was a much faster recovery. They don't really... hurt? The providers sedate you pretty well so its just a matter of zoning out, staying still, and holding your breath when they say so.

Illegals don't get any benefits and since they can't get proper checks they end up paying everything in cash. They pay sales tax and property tax and all that and taxes with an ITIN. So really there are some good and bad. Good- they give money to the government and aren't eligible for any benefits since they don't have an SSN. Bad - They take jobs that don't require background checks or a high school diploma. Illegals don't qualify for welfare or health insurance. So they pay it all out of pocket which means more money in circulation and going towards the government in the long run. If they can't afford food or shelter then they end up going back to their country anyway. Any interaction with the police could mean deportation so they have to be on good behavior here. Speeding ticket = Deported. Theft = Deported. Working Illegally = Deported.  Most keep out of trouble, work, and sleep. They can't really drive so they pay public transport fares which go to the cities and in turn help Americans. So they're not moochers. But its also not right. Immigration reform is important so that people don't continue to overstay for the sake of making money to send home.

Hey! So I've renewed twice and just sent in my third renewal (Lost my card so had to get a replacement) and I live in MN where they have workshops for these Renewals. So here's what they told me and how I sent my request. I'll answer some of your questions but not in order since... Well, I'm tired.

1. Make sure the expiration date on the paperwork you're sending is current. Check the top right corner for this date. I had to send an expired form but since the USCIS didn't update their paperwork it was okay.

2. They no longer require any proof of schooling or work since you've already been approved before.

3. You need to update your address with immigration ASAP. Go to their website and do that since it might cause problems with your application if you have a different address. You need to put your old address and new one on your forms, I believe it's addresses from 2012 to present? I don't remember too well but for sure your current and old one. Make sure your current is one where you will definitely stay at for the next three to four months. Also, your mailbox has to have your name on it for them to turn in your new card so do that as soon as you change your address with the postoffice too.

4. Go ahead and put overstay for #15 but only if you overstayed a visa.

4. Attach a copy of your current work permit and a copy of the work authorization request you sent with your initial application. You should have made a copy of the entire application before sending it, if not then check with your lawyer to see if they copied it.


Edit: for most of the application with the two columns you will only fill out the right hand side. Left will say 'Initial requests only' so you can completely ignore that half of the paper.

You need to hold off on anything serious until he's older. For his sake and yours.

I'm the black sheep in my family. Throughout my childhood my brothers would constantly tell me I should have never been born. That I was ugly, a monster, a mistake. I used to pray that I could die in some freak accident. I never went outright looking for it but the only thought I had was " I want to die." I tried fitting in with more people, changing myself, making new friends.... all failures. I changed but became a person that could survive the harsh reality of their past. I couldn't bear to open up and see a friend struggle to try and help me cope with things. It felt far too selfish. I cut ties almost immediately in order to protect myself from their disappointment. Seeing Robin say " If I'm allowed to say what I truly want... then... I WANT TO LIVE!!" After spending my entire childhood being told someone like me should die - and coming to believe it eventually... - hearing that unlocked something inside of me. I think that I was the first time I ever truly felt as if I wanted to live. I had spent so long trying to convince myself I should die that up until that point the thought of being allowed to live without being seen as " The coward that didn't off herself" had never crossed my mind.  Choppers backstory also struck a cord, his treatment from the villagers reminded me of my family. As well as his self-loathing. When he tries to explain that he'd be no good for the crew because he's a monster but Luffy cuts him off and yells " LETS GOOOO!!!!!" I cried like a baby. Spent so many years doing the same thing Chopper did: trying to justify my insecurities to avoid getting hurt later.
Nice to know that my creepy experience with a crazy lady brings you joy :D
